title: Innocent
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: A historical drama loosely based on the real Sanson family, hereditary executioners of Paris before the French Revolution. Gentle Charles-Henri Sanson recoils from the killing his inherited office demands but accepts it to protect his family, vowing to be the last executioner. His younger sister Marie-Joseph rebels against the gender rules of her time and seeks a place in the executions and at court.
life_message: It holds up refusing to let birth, office or society dictate who you are, even at great personal cost.

content.note: Graphic executions with heavy blood, a father torturing his son by breaking his legs, and animal cruelty (ANN reviews; Manga Critic; AniList Gore 81%, Torture 79%).
Unrelenting, lingering depictions of suffering and death; critics call it harsh and not for the faint of heart (ANN; Manga Critic; AniList Tragedy 85%).
Several sex scenes, a group-sex panel, implied rape and incest, frequent nudity (ANN publisher content warning and Silverman review; MangaUpdates Rape, Nudity; AniList Nudity 71%).
Dark Horse edition rated 18+ partly for language (Manga Critic); frequency not detailed (to verify).
Court and aristocratic debauchery suggests drinking; not singled out by reviews (to verify).
Child abuse, suicidal ideation and the psychological toll of executions on Charles-Henri (ANN reviews; Manga Critic on his paranoia and loneliness).
Historical torture and execution methods shown in detail; remote from daily life (to verify).
No product focus; no major merchandise tie-ins known.

delivery.note: Hereditary and royal order is shown as cruel through what it does to the characters.

winners_losers: Rigid hereditary and royal order is the loser, with sympathy for those who defy it, above all Marie-Joseph. Charles-Henri's conscience is respected, but the system that binds him is shown as cruel.
